hfrefEligibleDefault: No contraindications or cautions identified with the data provided.
hfrefLvefNote: Reported LVEF ({lvef}%) is above 40%. This module's criteria assume HFrEF (LVEF ≤ 40%).
hfrefDecompensationNote: Signs of decompensation present: prioritize clinical compensation before starting/up-titrating a beta-blocker; the other pillars can usually be started/continued as tolerated.
hfrefMissingDataNote: Fields left blank are not evaluated by the rules; fill in all data for a more complete assessment.
hfrefInsufficientClass: Eligibility for this class cannot be determined safely without the essential data (see "Missing data"). Requires clinical judgment once the data is complete.
hfrefHypoperfusionNote: Signs of hypoperfusion recorded: the chronic HFrEF flow may not be appropriate. Consider assessment in an acute/instability flow.
diureticPriorUser: On prior {agent} {oralDose} mg/day PO (≈ {furoEquiv} mg/day furosemide equivalent). Estimated initial IV dose ≈ 2.5× the daily oral dose = {total} mg/day IV furosemide, split into {doses} doses (~{perDose} mg per dose). Give at least twice daily and reassess response in 2–6 h.
diureticHighDoseSuffix: Caution: high dose (> {threshold} mg/day furosemide equivalent) with limited safety data.
diureticLoopNaive: Loop-diuretic-naive patient (or no oral dose provided). Suggested standard initial dose: furosemide {dose} mg IV bolus (usual range 40–80 mg). Reassess the diuretic response in ~2 h and continue at least twice daily if needed.
acuteIvJustification: Congestion present without severe hypoperfusion or hypotension — indication for an IV loop diuretic.
acuteIvNotes: IV doses should be given at least twice daily (post-dose sodium retention).
Reassess the response (diuresis/urine output) in 2–6 h and titrate the dose to the urine output goal.
Inadequate response/oliguria suggests diuretic resistance — consider intensification (sequential nephron blockade) and specialist evaluation.
acuteIvGeneralNote: The diuretic estimate is approximate and educational; individualize according to renal function, blood pressure and clinical response.
acuteSpecialistJustification: Congestion with hypoperfusion and/or hypotension (SBP < 90 mmHg) suggests low output. A diuretic alone may be insufficient or harmful.
acuteSpecialistNotes: Consider evaluation for inotropic/vasoactive support and monitoring. Out of scope for this flow (no cardiogenic shock).
An IV diuretic may be considered cautiously after hemodynamic stabilization.
acuteSpecialistGeneralNote: Scenario outside the scope of the simple diuretic flow — prioritize specialist evaluation.
acuteNoDiureticNoteDefault: An IV loop diuretic is not indicated in the absence of congestion. Reassess the diagnosis and volume status; optimize background therapy (GDMT) as indicated.
acuteNoDiureticNoteHypoperfusion: Hypoperfusion without congestion suggests hypovolemia/low output — specialist evaluation and reassessment of volume status.
acuteDiureticNeedsInfoJustification: Prior diuretic use was marked, but the agent and/or home dose were not provided — the IV dose cannot be estimated safely. Enter the diuretic and the daily dose to generate the estimate.
acuteInsufficientDataNote: Recommendation limited by missing data (see "Missing data"). Complete the data before deciding management.
acuteResistanceJustification: If the diuretic response is inadequate: reassess adherence, absorption, dose, residual congestion and renal function. Consider escalating the loop-diuretic dose and, per context and institutional protocol, sequential nephron blockade.
acuteResistanceNotes: Watch for hypokalemia, hyponatremia, worsening renal function and hypotension.
Reassess the response (diuresis, weight, fluid balance) after each adjustment.
acuteEquivalenceNote: Approximate loop-diuretic equivalences: furosemide 40 mg PO ≈ furosemide 20 mg IV ≈ torsemide 20 mg PO ≈ bumetanide 1 mg (PO/IV). Oral furosemide bioavailability ~50% (torsemide/bumetanide ~80–100%).
acuteGeneralNote: Flow restricted to congestion without cardiogenic shock. Continuously reassess blood pressure, perfusion and renal function.
